title: Change what is in yourselves
hookLine: Allah does not change a people's state until they change what is in themselves (13:11)

lines: GOD HELPS THOSE WHO HELP THEMSELVES?
cards: God helps those who help themselves. It sounds like scripture, and people quote it as if it were.
It isn't in the Qur'an, and it isn't in the Bible either; it's an old proverb that Benjamin Franklin's almanac helped make well-known.
But there's a verse in ar-Ra'd that people often reach for when they mean something like it, in speeches, in sermons, on classroom walls. Read slowly, it says something more searching.

teach.b: Verse eleven opens with a picture: every person has angels in front and behind, guarding them by God's command.
Then, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! Allah changeth not the condition of a folk until they (first) change that which is in their hearts".
In Arabic, the last words are ma bi-anfusihim: what is in themselves, in their own souls. Pickthall says hearts. Notice it's not about effort.

The proverb says: work hard, and God will help. The verse says: what's inside a people, their intentions, their habits of mind, their honesty, shapes what happens to them. The outer condition follows the inner one.
And it's plural: a folk, a people. Families, towns, nations, not just one person's self-improvement. Commentators point out the verse cuts both ways.
A similar verse in al-Anfal says God never changes a blessing He's given a people until they change what is in themselves.

teach.h: A PEOPLE, NOT JUST A PERSON.
teach.b: A people can lose a good condition by what they let grow inside them, just as they can rise by turning.
And the very next words in ar-Ra'd say that when God wills a hardship for a people, nothing can turn it back. So the verse isn't a guarantee that self-improvement brings success.
It's a statement about where change has to begin. Modern Muslim reformers have quoted it when calling their communities to inner renewal.

how: Muslim preachers and reformers often quote 13:11 when calling a community to inner renewal, and some teach it alongside 8:53 as a principle that a people's outward state follows its inward one.

games.q: a whole town is struggling. according to 13:11, where does a change in its condition begin?
o: with what is inside its people.
games.why: God does not change a people's condition until they change what is in themselves.

practice: Notice one habit of mind that shapes your days: a story you keep telling yourself, a suspicion you bring into every room, a habit of comparing or complaining.
Don't attack it; just see it clearly, and choose one small thought to put in its place. If you pray, ask God to help you change what is inside.

carryVoice: Your line: change starts inside. For a person, and for a whole people. Until tomorrow.
